course_name_original: Einführung in die Finite Differenzen und Finite Volumen Methoden
course_name_en: Introduction to Finite Difference and Finite Volume Methods
prerequisites: Differential and integral calculus of several variables

learning_outcomes.text: Students possess basic knowledge of numerical methods for solving partial differential equations.
They understand the concepts of consistency, stability, and convergence and can use them to evaluate numerical methods.
Students are able to numerically solve simple diffusion, advection, and advection-diffusion equations as well as elliptical equations time-dependently and in two dimensions.
They also know the fundamentals of the finite volume method and its application to selected model problems.
To be able to present the basic concepts of numerical methods for partial differential equations in a structured way.
To be able to explain precisely the terms consistency, stability, and convergence and to classify their meaning for numerical methods.
To be able to numerically solve simple diffusion and advection equations using appropriate time and space-discretized methods.
To be able to numerically treat elliptic equations for given boundary value problems with computational certainty.
To be able to formulate and solve time-dependent two-dimensional diffusion and advection-diffusion equations with appropriate numerical methods.
To be able to systematically analyze and compare numerical solution methods with regard to consistency, stability, and convergence properties.
To be able to explain the basic principles of the finite volume method and apply them appropriately to simple model problems.
To be able to communicate numerical results, model assumptions, and solution strategies professionally correct and comprehensible.
To be able to explain derivations, discretization approaches, and boundary conditions in partner and group settings in a structured manner.
To be able to critically reflect on numerical solution approaches and results and discuss them constructively.
To be able to independently work on simple numerical tasks and to structure the work process in a goal-oriented manner.
To be able to precisely document subject-specific mathematical notation, graphics, and results in written form.

syllabus_topics: Numerical solution of Laplace and Poisson equations
Numerical solution of the convection-diffusion equation
Introduction to the Finite Volume Method
